"""Failover From Scratch — the promotion a dead region never gets.

Ten graded stages over a world provided as data (`kv.py`, `topology.py`,
`fabric.py`, `scenarios.py`), the way the rest of this repository teaches
a mechanism: the world is data and holds the pinned truth, a stage is a
file you write, a check is what happens to it, and the fabric's own
replayed PINS table is the judge — because a failover you cannot fail
on schedule has exactly one authority, and a node's behavior is graded
by equality with it, one tick at a time.

What the course is about, in one line: *failover is a decision, never an
accident — and a decision is a majority with death notices, not a
timeout with a feeling.*

    the clock: ordering the versions, not the values
    the quorum: serve inside three or refuse entirely
    the hints: held for a peer, never served as yours
    anti-entropy: the union over ranges, never a choice
    health: a signal that is not a heartbeat
    sessions: the pinned answer is a table, not a feeling
    promotion: a majority adopted, or no epoch at all
    the redirect: a write applied exactly once
    late writes: reconcile, name the lost, price the RPO
    the drill: RTO/RPO measured, the foil run, the audit refused

The house laws hold here (`.h8-dev/CONTRACT.md` §1): standard library
only, no `float` anywhere — epochs, ticks, counters and clock entries
are ints the whole way —, no `math`, no `random`, no clock, no thread,
no socket, no wall-time ordering of anything a region can disagree on,
and a stage's job is pure state in, state out: the fabric drives the
network, the clocks and the failures, never the student.

What the course does **not** do is trust a heartbeat: the world sends
death notices on a watch channel, cuts stay SILENT, and the foil in
`naive.py` — same machine, wrong in exactly three places — runs the
same schedules so stage 10 can prove the divergences it names. Where
the lessons meet the paper (A6's hinted handoff and Merkle
anti-entropy, Dynamo's quorum arithmetic, H6's epoch fencing) lives in
the course's README — the drills are the practice half of the bargain.

    python3 codecraft/cli.py run failover-from-scratch
"""

                        ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__"))

                if name.startswith("stage_") and name.endswith(".py"):

                                 os.path.join(course, name))

        """`call()` must raise `exc` naming every string in `names`."""
        try:
            call()
        except exc as problem:
            text = str(problem)
            missing = [w for w in tuple(names) if w not in text]
            if missing:
                raise AssertionError(
                    "%s: refusal %r does not name %s"
                    % (what, text, missing))
        else:
            raise AssertionError("%s: no refusal" % (what,))

        must("after: v3 carries everything v1 does",
             s1.compare(v3, v1) == "after")
        must("before: mirrored", s1.compare(v1, v3) == "before")
        must("concurrent: siblings", s1.compare(v1, v2) == "concurrent")

        must("equal: a version with itself", s1.compare(v3, v3) == "equal")

        fact("equal is not after", s1.compare(v3, v3) != "after")
        fact("bumped clock is after, not equal",
             s1.compare(kv.version("a2", kv.bump(kv.clock_of(v1), "e1")),
                        v1) == "after")

        # --- coalesce: the survivor set
        must("Figure 3: four versions, exactly two siblings",
             s1.coalesce((v1, v2, v3, v4)) == (v3, v4))
        for perm in ((v4, v1, v3, v2), tuple(reversed((v1, v2, v3, v4))),
                     (v2, v4, v1, v3)):
            fact("coalesce ignores input order %r" % (perm,),
                 s1.coalesce(perm) == (v3, v4))
        must("coalesce(()) is ()", s1.coalesce(()) == ())
        must("exact duplicates are absorbed",
             s1.coalesce((v1, v2, v3, v4, v1, v3, v1)) == (v3, v4))
        fact("equal clocks with different values both survive",
             s1.coalesce((v3, kv.version("ab2", v3[2])))
             == (v3, kv.version("ab2", v3[2]))
             or s1.coalesce((v3, kv.version("ab2", v3[2])))
             == (kv.version("ab2", v3[2]), v3))
        fact("a single version survives alone", s1.coalesce((v2,)) == (v2,))
        fact("coalesce is idempotent",
             s1.coalesce(s1.coalesce((v1, v2, v3, v4))) == (v3, v4))

        # --- dominance_table: the check's evidence, sorted by the pair
        rows = s1.dominance_table((v1[2], v2[2], v3[2], v4[2]))
        must("table has one row per unordered pair", len(rows) == 6)
        must("rows sorted by the pair",
             rows == tuple(sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1]))))
        must("first and last row (clocks sort e1 < e1+e2 < e2 < e3)",
             (rows[0], rows[-1])
             == ((v1[2], v3[2], "before"),
                 (v2[2], v4[2], "concurrent")))
        fact("a shuffled caller gets the same sorted table",
             s1.dominance_table((v4[2], v2[2], v1[2], v3[2])) == rows)
        fact("the table carries the domination verdict",
             (v1[2], v3[2], "before") in rows)
        fact("two clocks answer one row",
             s1.dominance_table((v1[2], v1[2]))
             == ((v1[2], v1[2], "equal"),))

        # --- the refusal split: data is kv's, arguments are the stage's
        bad_version = ("h", "k", v1, "e1")
        bad_clock = (("e2", 1), ("e1", 1))
        unknown = ("v", "x", (("zz", 1),))
        _refuses(kv.KvError, "compare refuses malformed data",
                 lambda: s1.compare(bad_version, v1), names=())
        _refuses(kv.KvError, "compare refuses an unsorted clock",
                 lambda: s1.compare(v1, kv.version("x", bad_clock)),
                 names=())
        _refuses(kv.KvError, "coalesce refuses a node outside the fleet",
                 lambda: s1.coalesce((unknown,)), names=("zz",))
        _refuses(kv.KvError, "the table refuses a malformed clock",
                 lambda: s1.dominance_table((bad_clock, v1[2])), names=())
        _refuses(s1.FailError, "the table refuses one clock",
                 lambda: s1.dominance_table((v1[2],)), names=("1",))
        _refuses(s1.FailError, "the table refuses no clocks",
                 lambda: s1.dominance_table(()), names=("0",))
        fact("determinism", s1.coalesce((v1, v2, v3, v4))
             == s1.coalesce((v1, v2, v3, v4)))

        if problems:
            raise AssertionError("%d facts failed" % (len(problems),))
        print("check_01: PASS (%d facts)" % (facts,))
        return 0
    finally:
        if root:
            sys.path[:] = [p for p in sys.path if p != course]
            shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)

"""kv.py — the version grammar (provided world).

A version is `("v", value, clock)`; a clock is a tuple of `(node,
counter)` pairs sorted by node, distinct, counters >= 0; the value is an
opaque string. That is the whole storage shape A6 described, with the
floats and the objects removed: clocks are DATA, and a stage can hold
one wrong at most.

The world ships `dominates` only — the four-way comparison and the
sibling coalescing are the student's stage 1, because the fabric itself
never orders versions. Constructors refuse every malformed shape with
`KvError`, naming the offender: a clock that is unsorted, has a
duplicate node, a negative counter, or a value that is not a string
never reaches a scenario.
"""

from topology import NODES

KIND_VERSION = "v"
KIND_HINT = "hint"

VALID_NODES = tuple(sorted(n for n, _ in NODES))


class KvError(ValueError):
    """The world's refusal: a version, clock, or hint that is not shaped right."""


def _check_clock(clock):
    if not isinstance(clock, tuple):
        raise KvError("kv: a clock must be a tuple, got %r" % (type(clock).__name__,))
    prev = None
    for entry in clock:
        if (not isinstance(entry, tuple) or len(entry) != 2
                or not isinstance(entry[0], str) or not isinstance(entry[1], int)):
            raise KvError("kv: a clock entry must be a (node, int) pair, got %r"
                          % (entry,))
        node, counter = entry
        if node not in VALID_NODES:
            raise KvError("kv: clock names %r, which is not in the fleet %s"
                          % (node, ", ".join(VALID_NODES)))
        if counter < 0:
            raise KvError("kv: clock counter for %s is %d, below 0" % (node, counter))
        if prev is not None and node <= prev:
            raise KvError("kv: clock entries must be sorted by node and distinct, "
                          "got %r after %r" % (node, prev))
        prev = node
    return clock


def version(value, clock):
    """`("v", value, clock)`; value an opaque string, clock checked."""
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise KvError("kv: a version's value must be a string, got %r"
                      % (type(value).__name__,))
    return (KIND_VERSION, value, _check_clock(clock))


def clock_of(v):
    """The version's clock."""
    _check_version(v)
    return v[2]


def value_of(v):
    """The version's opaque value."""
    _check_version(v)
    return v[1]


def _check_version(v):
    if (not isinstance(v, tuple) or len(v) != 3 or v[0] != KIND_VERSION
            or not isinstance(v[1], str)):
        raise KvError("kv: a version must be ('v', value:str, clock), got %r" % (v,))
    _check_clock(v[2])
    return v


def bump(clock, node):
    """The clock with `node`'s counter +1 (absent node becomes (node, 1)).
    The write side of A6's increment; stays immutable and sorted."""
    _check_clock(clock)
    if node not in VALID_NODES:
        raise KvError("kv: bump names %r, which is not in the fleet %s"
                      % (node, ", ".join(VALID_NODES)))
    entries = dict(clock)
    entries[node] = entries.get(node, 0) + 1
    return tuple(sorted(entries.items()))


def dominates(a, b):
    """True iff every counter in `b` is present in `a` and >=. Equal clocks
    dominate each other; the four-way law (before/after/equal/concurrent)
    is stage 1's to derive from this primitive."""
    _check_clock(a)
    _check_clock(b)
    da = dict(a)
    return all(da.get(node, 0) >= counter for node, counter in b)


def hint(key, ver, intended_for):
    """`("hint", key, version, intended_for)` — a write parked on a node
    that a peer could not reach. Held, never owned: serving it as yours
    is stage 3's refusal."""
    if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
        raise KvError("kv: a hint's key must be a non-empty string, got %r" % (key,))
    _check_version(ver)
    if intended_for not in VALID_NODES:
        raise KvError("kv: a hint intended_for %r, which is not in the fleet %s"
                      % (intended_for, ", ".join(VALID_NODES)))
    return (KIND_HINT, key, ver, intended_for)

"""topology.py — the fleet as pure data (provided world).

Two regions, three nodes each, independent clocks. `TICK_RATE = 2` means
west is ticked once per two global ticks: a number one region stamps can
never be compared with a number the other stamps, which is why ordering
anything that can cross the link takes the vector clock (stage 1) or the
epoch (stage 7) and never a stamp. `LAG_BOUND` is the applied-count a
healthy node may trail the region's best by and still count toward a
quorum — the health signal is servability, not presence.

Everything here is tuples, strings and ints: the shape of the failure is
data, so every scenario is reproducible.
"""


REGIONS = ("east", "west")

NODES = (("e1", "east"), ("e2", "east"), ("e3", "east"),
         ("w1", "west"), ("w2", "west"), ("w3", "west"))

# The primary region at tick 0 and its epoch: the world's starting truth.
# Promotion (stage 7) is the only way this changes, and the fabric fences
# old epochs forever after.
PRIMARY = "east"
INITIAL_EPOCH = 1

# West ticks once per two global ticks: independent clocks, in operation.
TICK_RATE = 2

# A healthy node's applied_count may trail the region's best observed by
# at most this many writes. PINS-bound: stage 5's rule, not a tunable.
LAG_BOUND = 2

_BY_ID = dict(NODES)


def region_of(node_id):
    """The region a node id lives in; unknown ids refuse with a name."""
    if node_id not in _BY_ID:
        raise ValueError("topology: unknown node id %r (fleet is %s)"
                         % (node_id, ", ".join(sorted(_BY_ID))))
    return _BY_ID[node_id]


def nodes_of(region):
    """The region's node ids, sorted — the entry node is the first live one."""
    if region not in REGIONS:
        raise ValueError("topology: unknown region %r (fleet is %s)"
                         % (region, ", ".join(REGIONS)))
    return tuple(sorted(n for n, r in NODES if r == region))


def peers_of(node_id):
    """The same region's OTHER nodes, sorted. A node never hears from the
    other region except across the link, and that is the fabric's business."""
    region = region_of(node_id)
    return tuple(n for n in nodes_of(region) if n != node_id)


def majority(n):
    """H6's law, restated: a decision needs n // 2 + 1, an int, never a
    fraction. majority(3) == 2 and majority(2) == 2."""
    if not isinstance(n, int) or n < 0:
        raise ValueError("topology: majority needs an int >= 0, got %r"
                         % (n,))
    return n // 2 + 1

"""The tiny API an authored course uses to describe its stages.

A course is a directory containing `course.py`:

    from codecraft.api import stage

    TITLE = "Build a Bloom Filter"
    DESCRIPTION = "A probabilistic set, from hashing to false-positive math."

    def check_1():
        from bloom import BloomFilter
        bf = BloomFilter(bits=64, hashes=2)
        bf.add("x")
        assert "x" in bf
        assert "y" not in bf, "a fresh filter must not report false members"

    STAGES = [
        stage(
            1,
            file="bloom.py",
            title="add and contains",
            tags=["hashing", "data-structure"],
            action="Implement add() to set the k bit positions.",
            predict="can contains() ever be certain an item is absent?",
            hints=["bits = bits[:] to avoid shared state",
                   "use one hash salt per position"],
            check=check_1,
        ),
        ...
    ]

`codecraft run <course>` imports this file, runs each `check`, records the
attempt, and hands the result to the adaptive engine. `hints` are optional —
when omitted, the engine generates them from `action`/`predict`.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional


@dataclass
class Stage:
    id: int
    file: str
    title: str
    check: Callable[[], None]
    tags: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    action: str = ""
    predict: str = ""
    hints: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    solution: Optional[str] = None   # e.g. "solutions/bloom.py: BloomFilter.add"

    def meta(self) -> Dict[str, object]:
        return {
            "file": self.file,
            "title": self.title,
            "tags": list(self.tags),
            "action": self.action,
            "predict": self.predict,
            "hints": list(self.hints),
            "solution": self.solution,
        }


def stage(id: int, file: str, title: str, check: Callable[[], None],
          tags: Optional[List[str]] = None, action: str = "", predict: str = "",
          hints: Optional[List[str]] = None,
          solution: Optional[str] = None) -> Stage:
    """Convenience constructor so course.py stays readable."""
    return Stage(
        id=id, file=file, title=title, check=check, tags=list(tags or []),
        action=action, predict=predict, hints=list(hints or []),
        solution=solution,
    )
